title: Inner Lookup Run
statement: Let $mode$ be a Boolean mode, let $u$ and $b'$ be bit strings, and let $q$ be a natural number satisfying $q\le 2|\langle\langle u,b'\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(q)\rangle|$, where $\mathrm{bits}(q)$ is the binary bit string for $q$. Set $h=\langle\langle u,b'\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(q)\rangle$ and $z=\langle u,b'\rangle$. Starting on input $h$ in state $copy(4,false)$, with register values $ptr=4|u|+4$, $zend=2|z|$, $query=q$, $tail=2|z|+2$, and all other registers zero, the machine halts with the length test $q<|dropIdx(z)|$ when $mode$ is true, and otherwise with the bit of $dropIdx(z)$ at position $q$, defaulting to false if out of range. Every configuration before halting satisfies the machine's safety condition and register bound.
hypotheses_covered: mode is a Boolean machine mode
u and b' are bit strings
q is at most twice the length of the paired input encoding
